_about.what: Real-world size table for the realism rule 'size as in life' (PLAN-REALISM.md §6.1). Checked by tools/qa/realism-rules.mjs → rule 'sizes'.

measure.h: height: world AABB y-extent of the Passport entry (drawn triangles, world space)
measure.l: length: long side of the minimum-area rectangle around the entry's vertices seen from above (rotation-independent)
measure.w: width: short side of that rectangle
measure.trunkH: tree height: top of the trunk collider (bark part of the model, instance scale) above its base — ≈ the tree height for spruces
measure.stature: pilot: skinned-vertex height in idle (boots to top of head/helmet)
measure.shoulder: quadruped: height of the withers (highest spine/neck-base bone over the front feet) above the lowest hoof/paw

_about.tolerance: ranges are [min, max] in metres. Where a single real value is known the range is that value ±15 % (PLAN-REALISM §6); where nature varies, the observed range.
_about.match: key = Passport kind (entry name without #n) or actor id; 'match' (regex) extends a row to several kinds

pilot.src: adult male stature + boots/helmet; ANSUR II (US Army 2012) male mean 1.755 m, 95th pct 1.87 m

fox.src: arctic fox 25–30 cm, red fox 35–50 cm at the shoulder (Larivière & Pasitschniak-Arts 1996, Mammalian Species 537)

stag.src: reindeer / caribou shoulder height 0.85–1.5 m, adult bull ~1.1–1.3 m (Rangifer tarandus, Banfield 1961 / ADF&G)

kestrel.src: wreck fuselage = Douglas DC-3 / C-47: length 19.66 m (64 ft 8 in) ±15 %

st_tent_dome.src: polar camp tents: Scott/pyramid tent ~2.1–2.4 m, Arctic Oven 10 peak 2.1 m, Weatherhaven 2.4 m; ≥ 1.9 m so a person stands

crate.src: wooden / military transport crates 0.4–0.8 m high (NATO ammo & ration boxes 0.3–0.6, cargo crates to 0.8)

drum.src: 200 l (55 US gal) steel drum: 0.88 m tall, 0.57–0.61 m diameter (ISO 15750)

barrel_steel.src: 200 l drum lying on its side: length 0.88 m, diameter 0.57–0.61 m

lamp_post.src: camp / site lamp pole 2.5–6 m, street lamp 4–8 m

wf_flag_pole.src: survey / route marker flags on 1–3 m bamboo poles

struct_hab_module.src: containerised polar hab module: ISO container 2.6 m × 6.1/12.2 m; Halley VI modules ~4–6 m high on legs

station_dome.src: geodesic station dome (Amundsen–Scott 1975 dome 16 m high, 50 m wide)

st_snowcat.src: PistenBully 600: 2.8–3.1 m high, 5.5–8.5 m long (with blade)

vehicle_rover_sev.src: NASA Space Exploration Vehicle / polar rover: ~3–4 m high, 4.5–6 m long

st_sledge.src: Nansen sledge 2.4–4 m long, 0.3 m frame, loaded up to ~1.3 m

st_rowboat.src: wooden rowboat 3–5 m long, 0.5–1 m high

st_inuksuk.src: inuksuit are usually 1–2 m (rarely up to several m)

firepit.src: stone fire ring 0.9–1.5 m across, stones 0.15–0.4 m

iceberg_small.src: bergy bit 1–5 m above the water (WMO sea-ice nomenclature)

pressure_ridge.src: sea-ice pressure ridge sails typically 1–3 m, rarely > 5 m

boulder.src: flat slabs from 0.1 m, boulders ≥ 0.26 m (Wentworth); glacial erratics up to several m — sanity bound only

tree_spruce_krummholz.src: krummholz spruce at the tree line 0.5–3 m

tree_spruce_snowladen.src: snow-laden taiga spruce (Picea obovata / glauca) 5–20 m

tree_spruce_tall_snow.src: mature spruce 10–30 m (Picea abies up to 35–50 m)

tree_fir_windbent.src: wind-shaped subalpine fir (Abies lasiocarpa) 3–15 m at exposed sites

tree_dead_birch.src: downy birch (Betula pubescens) at the northern limit 3–15 m

fantasy: not checked (no real-world size): st_crystal_tree, st_rift_crystal, st_rift_cluster, spire*, echo*, orm, st_ruin_*, wf_ice, debris, kestrel_wing, kestrel_tail, ice_chunk, st_pier, st_pole_fallen
